newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: OPTIONS -- PHILIPS OPTIONS IN DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -- PHILIPS OPTIONS IN DEMAND.

text.p: Demand for Philips Electronics options soared in early Wednesday afternoon, reflecting rises in the cash market.
Philips stock rose 2.00 guilders to 64.80 each at 1240 GMT.
"As a result of the steady advance of the stock, demand in options increased," said one dealer, adding that a 65.00 guilder resistance level was in sight.
Dealers said Philips was profiting from Tuesday's U.S. book-to-bill ratio announcement, a key indicator for the semiconductor industry. The ratio rose to 0.99 in September from 0.93 in August.

Philips accounted for just over six percent of trade on the Amsterdam options bourse this morning, but volumes later increased rapidly and by 1245 GMT Philips options made up nearly 20 percent of total volume.
Most business was in October calls at a 65 guilder strike at an 80 cent premium.
"I see the stock rising to 68-69 guilders within a couple of weeks," said another dealer, adding this was just ahead of the group's third quarter results, due on October 24.
